questions.question: Which heading tag is the largest and most important?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <h1> is the largest and most important heading. HTML has six heading levels (<h1> to <h6>), with <h1> being the main title of the page.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <h1> is the largest and most important heading. HTML has six heading levels (<h1> to <h6>), with <h1> being the main title of the page.

questions.question: How many <h1> tags should you typically use on one page?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: You should typically have only ONE <h1> per page, just like a book has one title. This helps screen readers and search engines understand your page structure.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: You should typically have only ONE <h1> per page, just like a book has one title. This helps screen readers and search engines understand your page structure.

questions.question: Which tag is used for regular text paragraphs?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: The <p> tag (short for 'paragraph') is used for regular text blocks. It automatically adds spacing before and after the text.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: The <p> tag (short for 'paragraph') is used for regular text blocks. It automatically adds spacing before and after the text.

questions.question: Which is the correct order of heading importance?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Headings go from most important (<h1>) to least important (<h6>). The number gets bigger as importance decreases.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Headings go from most important (<h1>) to least important (<h6>). The number gets bigger as importance decreases.

questions.question: Which heading would be appropriate for a chapter title?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <h2> is perfect for chapter titles or major sections. <h1> is for the book title (main page title), and <h2> is for chapters within that book.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <h2> is perfect for chapter titles or major sections. <h1> is for the book title (main page title), and <h2> is for chapters within that book.

questions.question: What happens if you skip heading levels (e.g., go from <h1> to <h3>)?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Skipping heading levels (like going from <h1> to <h3> without an <h2>) is bad for accessibility. Screen readers use heading structure to help visually impaired users navigate.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Skipping heading levels (like going from <h1> to <h3> without an <h2>) is bad for accessibility. Screen readers use heading structure to help visually impaired users navigate.

questions.question: Which tag creates the smallest heading?

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: <h6> creates the smallest heading. All heading tags (<h1> to <h6>) create bold text, but <h6> is the smallest size.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: <h6> creates the smallest heading. All heading tags (<h1> to <h6>) create bold text, but <h6> is the smallest size.

correct.details: True! <p> tags automatically add vertical spacing (margins) before and after paragraphs, creating natural separation between text blocks.

questions.question: What is the purpose of heading hierarchy?
options: To make the page look pretty

correct.title: Correct! 🎉
correct.details: Heading hierarchy helps organize content logically - like an outline for your page. It helps users (and search engines) understand the structure and importance of information.

wrong.title: Not quite! 🤔
wrong.details: Heading hierarchy helps organize content logically - like an outline for your page. It helps users (and search engines) understand the structure and importance of information.

correct.details: <p> tags provide structure and accessibility. They tell browsers, screen readers, and search engines that this is a paragraph of text, not just random words.
